title: Gift Exchange versus Monetary Exchange: Theory and Evidence
central_claims: In the laboratory Lagos–Wright setting, subjects select monetary rather than efficient gift-exchange equilibria.
Money increases achieved welfare compared with an otherwise comparable no-money setting, acting as a coordination device.

sources.title: Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics: supplementary materials, Tables S1–S2
sources.finding: The six-person money-versus-no-money welfare contrast did not replicate: N=96, p=.674, r=-.12, versus original N=54 and r=.76. This directly concerns the selected welfare comparison, not every theoretical result.

sources.title: On the monetary exchange with multiple equilibrium money holdings distributions: An experimental approach
sources.finding: Kamiya, Kobayashi, Shichijo and Shimizu study a different divisible-money model, compare its outcomes with Duffy/Puzzello, and report rare gift giving and efficient endogenous monetary exchange. Read publisher abstract, introduction and section text available through search indexing; direct retrieval was blocked.

search_gaps: Original reading was the complete publisher abstract, not full text.
A different monetary model is not a direct reproduction or demonstrated use of this specific experimental construction.
The live study07 replication link redirects to a website containing unrelated material; numerical evidence instead comes from the archived primary supplement.
No reliable operational-adoption, systematic-synthesis or newer-alternative evidence was established.
summary: The selected welfare advantage failed a larger replication. A later independent experiment substantively compares the paper while studying a different monetary model. That related evidence cannot resolve the original welfare contrast or establish universal failure.
